course_description:
Overview of policy development process as it is applied to conservation & environmental management. Conservation policy in both international & national context. (Minimum enrolment required 8)

In this course we study important conservation policy frameworks, considering their development, implementation and evaluation. The focus is primarily on public policy at international, national and sub-national levels.

Policy development occurs in a social arena of contending rights and interests, beliefs and viewpoints. Through the lens of current policy debates, we explore the social, economic and political conditions that either aid or impede the development of good conservation policy. In particular, we delve into the Australian political and governmental system to understand the context within which conservation policy develops and changes.

At theﾠinternational level we study major conservation conventions, such as the UN Conventionﾠon Biological Diversity (CBD), World Heritage, RAMSARﾠand CITES. We explore how these international commitments are translated to national policy frameworks and the effectiveness of those frameworks, using examples such as Australia's Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation Act .

We examine policy responses to the need to protect threatened species and ecological communities, the species and environments of the open seas and protected areas like the Great Barrier Reef.

The course draws in experts in conservation policy and practitioners with extensive experience in designing and implementing policy. We discuss practicalities and processes of policy development: who forms policy and why, and what steps have to be taken and issues have to be accounted for in developing policy? We debate topical policy issues and learn through evaluating existing policy and developing policy briefs focussed on real-world conservation issues.

course_aims: The aims of this course are to build an understanding of the various international and national policies and policy instruments most relevant to conservation policy and how they interact, to analyse the strengths and weaknesses of those policies, to appreciate the social and political content in which policies are made and succeed or fail, to develop critical skills in policy evaluation, and to understand drivers, processes and challenges for conservation policy development and implementation.

learning_outcomes.description: Identify and explain the main conservation policy instruments and frameworks at international and national levels, and how they interact.
Articulate the policy development process and identify constraints on development and implementation of conservation policy
For a given conservation problem, identify alternative policy responses, and analyze their respective strengths and weaknesses.
Prepare credible, concise and evidence-informed policy positions/briefs on conservation issues, considering its socio-political context and other relevant issues.
Analyse the effectiveness of a policy, and identify and articulate ways to improve policy effectiveness within a set of real-world constraints.
Place common policy debates held in the public arena within their policy frameworks and identify motivations of stakeholders and interest groups in those debates.
Anticipate and critically appraise likely impacts, both intended and unintended, positive and negative, of proposed policy approaches in different contexts

Argue persuasively for and justify specific formulations of international policy statements, and connect current events together to improve appreciation of challenges to international policy effectiveness

assessment_details.title: Policy review plan
assessment_details.task_description: Following the Samuel review of the EPBC Act in 2020, there have been several proposed government policy responses. Several of these have been at least partly initiated, including changes to biodiversity offsetting, a new Nature Repair Market, and the foundations of new bioregional planning approaches. For Assignment 2, you will prepare a full review of ONE of these policy initiatives. For this Assignment 1, you will prepare an outline of this full review, including a timeline of key policy developments and an annotated bibliography of key resources. Feedback received will support the development of your full review in Assignment 2. For Assignment 1, select one of the three Australian Federal policy initiatives about which the course staff will provide information and some key documentation: either bioregional planning, the Nature Repair Market, or biodiversity offsetting. Identify the policy’s objectives and the mechanism though which it seeks to achieve them, and research this type of policy instrument as well as the progression of the policy from at least the Samuel Review to the current day. Prepare a plan for your Assignment 2 that includes: · An outline of the sections that your Assignment 2 will include · A one-paragraph description of the policy and its objectives · A draft timeline in figure format, covering at least the period 2020-2026, indicating key milestones in the policy development process · An annotated bibliography of at least ten key resources that you will draw on for your policy review. These should include peer-reviewed literature, relevant government documents, and sources of stakeholder perspectives. Submit via Turnitin by the due date a written report of maximum 1000 words, including the annotated bibliography, but not including text within the timeline figure. assessment_details.title: Full policy review
assessment_details.task_description: Following the Samuel review of the EPBC Act in 2020, there have been several proposed government policy responses. Several of these have been at least partly initiated, including changes to biodiversity offsetting, a new Nature Repair Market, and the foundations of new bioregional planning approaches. For Assignment 2, prepare a full review of ONE of these policy initiatives. You may include revised (if necessary) versions of the text and timeline included in Assignment 1. For Assignment 2, select one of the three Australian Federal policy initiatives about which the course staff will provide information and some key documentation: either bioregional planning, the Nature Repair Market, or biodiversity offsetting. Prepare a report that includes: · A one-paragraph description of the policy and its objectives · An explanation of the type of policy instrument or instruments it employs, and a short critical review of these instrument types drawing on peer-reviewed and other literature including a section identifying its relevance to the Global Biodiversity Framework goals and targets · A timeline in figure format, covering at least the period 2020-2026, indicating key milestones in the development of this specific policy in Australia · A summary of public critique, stakeholder perspectives and concerns regarding this policy during its development · A well-reasoned analysis of the major risks and potential benefits of the policy as currently formulated, requirements for it to be effective, and recommendations for any changes, improvements, or safeguards Submit via Turnitin by the due date a written report of maximum 2800 words, not including the reference list or text within the timeline figure. assessment_details.title: Policy briefing
assessment_details.task_description: Identify a conservation challenge and a policy response that you believe would help to address it. It can be from any jurisdiction in the world, but it must be a different issue that the one you examined in Assignments 1 and 2. Imagine you are a policy advisor to the government Minister who would be primarily responsible for enacting this policy. Your role is to inform the Minister about the issue and proposed policy response in the form of a policy brief and a short spoken pitch, during which the Minister (your tutor) will ask you questions. Prepare: 1) a succinct one-page policy brief using the template provided (with references), 2) a 300-word proposal for how the effectiveness of this policy would be evaluated after five years of its operation; and 3) a convincing persuasive spoken overview of the brief of one minute only. Submit the written component as one document via Turnitin by the due date. Your spoken briefing will be presented in class in weeks 12 and 13. You will be graded on the written component, the persuasiveness and clarity of the spoken component, and your ability to respond effectively to the questions asked by your tutor. In addition to submitting the written component, you must attend tutorials in Weeks 12 AND 13, and be ready to give your presentation and response to questions when called upon (unless alternative arrangements approved in advance) Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Translation (MT) Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Translation (MT) are emerging tools that may support students in completing this assessment task.
